verdicts.gapA: A is not a state screen at all — it is a tilted marketing mock with the headline "Save your favorite articles" pasted over a device frame, and the sheet beneath is cropped so the body text truncates mid-word at the right edge ("The **Solar System**[a] is t", "bound planetary systen", "Of the obje"). Nothing here shows an empty, loading, or error condition, offers a retry, or names a next action beyond the generic "Create new" row; showing one complete, uncropped screen that actually depicts the empty case with a labeled action would be the single change that could move the pick.
verdicts.gapB: The explanatory card states the blocker — "Pas encore de cote R : les bourses qui en dépendent apparaîtront après ta première session" — but the only action it offers is "Modifier mes étiquettes", which does not answer the blocker it just raised; a first-session student is told what is missing and then handed an unrelated button. Naming the action that matches the copy (e.g. filtering to the bursaries that are open now, or setting a reminder for end of session) would close it; secondarily, the screenshot shows only the empty variant, so the skeleton-geometry and error-retry halves of the criterion are unverifiable from this frame.
violationsA: Truncated text throughout the sheet: "The Solar System[a] is t", "bound planetary systen", "the objects that orbit it,", "indirectly.[b] Of the obje", "Sun directly, the largest" — every line is cut at the right edge
violationsB: The "source" chip beside "Vérifié le 24 août 2026 ·" reads as a tappable link but measures roughly 20 CSS px tall — well under the 44px minimum; the "Postuler" and "Modifier mes étiquettes" pills are themselves only borderline at ~40px
verdicts.notes: B is the only one of the two that behaves like a product screen: figures carry provenance in place ("500 $ – 1 000 $" over "Fondation du Cégep de Sainte-Foy", "Vérifié le 24 août 2026 · source"), no copy recommends a programme or predicts admission, and the empty case is explained rather than left blank. Its craft is clean — clear "Bourses" > cégep > banner > "Admissible maintenant" ladder, consistent card rhythm, legible at arm's length — though the second card is sliced by the tab bar with a button half-hidden behind it, which reads as a rendering fault rather than a scroll edge. A is a store-listing graphic, not a screen under test, and fails the criterion on every visible count.

verdicts.gapA: Top bar, left half: the wordmark and the session chip are drawn on top of each other — "MaCote" has a stray "R" stacked above and a ":" below, running straight into "31,20 CONFIRMÉE" with no gap. The single most important element of this shell (the cote R chip) is the one thing you cannot read; give the chip its own padded pill separated from the logo and A likely takes the round, because everything below it (sourcing, verification dates, labelled tabs) is stronger than B.
verdicts.gapB: The red nav block: four tabs (flame, feed-with-play, TV, bookmark) plus an eye and a "?" in the app bar are icon-only, zero text. Nothing tells a first-time user what any of them opens — the "eye" in particular is unguessable — and the underline only says which unnamed thing is active; put a word under each tab and the nav stops being a guessing game.
violationsA: Overlapping text in the top bar: the logo lettering ('MaCote' with a stacked 'R' and ':') collides with the session chip '31,20 CONFIRMÉE', leaving both illegible — a direct hit on 'no overlapping text'.

The figure '31,20' in the top-bar chip is shown with the claim 'CONFIRMÉE' but no source and no verification date beside it; the sourcing only appears further down the page, so the chip alone reads as an unattributed confirmed number.

Bottom tab bar is cramped to roughly the 44-48px floor with labels ('MA COTE', 'PROGRAMMES', 'BOURSES', 'PROFIL') sitting flush against the bottom edge — no safe-area padding, so real targets are at or under the limit.

The mini player overlays and clips the last feed item — 'The Mozilla Community Call' row's '136 views • 6 days ago' and thumbnail are half-covered, i.e. overlapping content with no reserved list padding.
verdicts.notes: A is the better-behaved product on substance — every figure carries 'Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · source' or 'Saisie par toi le 28 août 2026', tabs are worded, the active tab is unmistakable — but its shell fails at the one place it is being judged: the top bar is a legibility car crash, and a broken masthead is the first and worst thing a user meets. B is generic and lazy about naming things (six unlabelled icons) and lets its mini player eat the last row, yet its bar, tab row and list rhythm hold together at arm's length with nothing garbled. I pick B narrowly on execution, not ambition; fix the collision in A's header and my pick flips.

verdicts.notes: A actually delivers the brief — three grouped caps headers, a search field ("Cherche ton programme ou son code"), and the profile step explained in one line ("Si ton programme a des profils, tu le préciseras à l'étape suivante") — while B answers a different question well but breaks two hard rules. A's craft is nonetheless mediocre: a ~20-item first group with no anchors beyond tiny grey headers, code text so light it dies at arm's length, and an unexplained disabled CTA at the end of a very long scroll. B has the better typographic hierarchy and the better per-row copy (each option carries a plain one-line definition), and A should steal exactly that idea for its rows.

verdicts.notes: A meets its stated bar — the caveat is a fixed, undismissible block, the ≈ total and dashed frame are always on screen, and the bottom-anchored caveat/total/CTA stack means added rows should grow into the empty middle rather than shove the total off-screen — but it wins on honesty more than on craft. Its real faults are hierarchy (caveat outweighs the number it qualifies), three identical "Ex : Philosophie 101" placeholders doing duty as labels so meaning vanishes once typing starts, and three competing accents (black pill, blue link, lavender CTA that reads disabled next to a copy conflict: "Estimation actuelle" already live vs a button promising "Estimer ma cote"). verdicts.notes: A earns the pick on the criterion, not on craft: every programme carries a "SUGGÉRÉ" badge, a "Vérifié le 25 août 2026" date, a source chip and a visible "Ta cote: 31,20 · saisie par toi", and the three choices plus "Passer cette étape" are legible and correctly ordered — but the page is a ten-screen scroll of 10–11px reference prose, the university names under each title are lighter than their badges so near-identical duplicate cards are hard to tell apart, and "Passer cette étape" is grey text that neither looks tappable nor says that skipping saves nothing. verdicts.notes: B is the only one of the two that is actually the screen in question, and it does the hard part well — four rows each with a plain-language consequence, and the line "Enregistré sur cet appareil. Connecte-toi pour retrouver ces choix sur tes autres appareils." states offline persistence and the guest state in one breath, with no push section pretending to exist. A is a store-marketing composition ("Customizable / Many customization options, encryption and backups") wrapped around an unrelated Appearance list, so roughly 40% of the canvas carries no product and the product it does carry is cropped. B's remaining faults are honesty faults, not layout ones: a header score labelled CONFIRMÉE with no date next to it, and a footer that promises a verification date it never shows.
